18.en: Having heard of Rama's hermitage on the Chitrakuta mountain inhabited by pious men, magnanimous Bharata, commanded his army to stay at a distance, and quickly proceeded with Guha. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टनवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyeighth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
18.hi: हे वैदेही ! मेरे साथ चित्रकूट पवत पर मन, वचन और देह को बश में कर!लेने बाले इन विविध साधनों को देख, तेरा मन प्रसन्न होता है कि नहीं ?

20.hi: देखो, इस पबत की सेकड़ां विशाल शिलाएँ, नीली, पीली सफेद आदि विविध रंगों की हें; चारों ओर कैसी शोभा दे रही हें

21.hi: cf UE Ef J Se! MSS ESE Me MSS १ अमृतप्राहुः-मोक्षसाधनं प्राहुः । ( रा० ) २ प्रेत्यभवार्थाय-- :देवादिदेहान्तरपरिग्ररूपप्रयोजनाय च प्राहुः | (गो०) इस पव त पर उत्पन्न हजारों बूटियाँ, रात के समय अपनी प्रभा से दीष्त हो, अम्निशिखा की तरह प्रकाश कर, शोभायमान होती हैं

22.hi: हे भामिनि ! देखो इस पव त पर कोई मा तो घर जैसा, कोई फुलवाडी जेसा और कोई स्थान एक ही शिला का दिखलाई पड़ता है। ये सभी इस पर्वत की शोभा को बढाने वाले हैं

23.hi: ऐसा जान पड़ता है मानों यह चित्रकूट पर्वत पुथिवी को फोड़ कर निकला हो । इस प॑वत का अग्रभाग चारों ओर से कैसा सुहावना जान पड़ता है

24.hi: हे भद्रे ! कामी लोगों के इन विछौनां को तो देखो । इनके नीचे तो कमलों के पत्ते विछें हैं और पत्तों के ऊपर कूट, पुत्रजीवक और भोजपत्र की छाले विद्धी हुई हें.

25.hi: ₹वास्तरान्‌--शयनानीत्यर्थः | (गो०) यह देखो कामी जनों की पहनी हुई और कुम्हलाई तथा त्यागी हुई कमल के फूलों की मालाएँ, इधर उधर पड़ी हैं और उन लोगों के खाए हुए अनेक प्रकार के फल पड़े हैं

26.hi: विविध प्रकार के कन्द फल और स्वच्छ जल सम्पन्न चित्रकूट पब त ने, रमणीयता में कुवेर की अलकापुरी, इन्द्र की अमरावती और उत्तर कुरुदेश को मात कर दिआ है

1.sa: निविष्टायां तु सेनायामुत्सुको भरतस्तदा।जगाम भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं शत्रुध्नमनुदर्शयन् ॥ २.९९.१॥
1.en: Eager to see his brother, Bharata encamped the army and set out showing the hermitage to Satrughna.
1.hi: कुलधम:--प्रजापालन । (गो० ) Vin ०पश्चनवतिहम $/8 सग?” onations अथ शेलाद्विनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलीं कोसलेरप्ररः । अदर्शयच्छुभजलां रम्यां मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्‌

2.sa: ऋषिं वसिष्ठं सन्दिश्य मातऽर्मे शीघ्रमानय।इति त्वरितमग्रे स जगाम गुरुवत्सल: ॥ २.९९.२॥
2.en: Bharata, deeply devoted towards elders, indicated to sage Vasistha to bring along the mothers, and proceeded ahead quickly.
2.hi: कमलनयन श्रीरामचन्द्र चन्द्रमा के समान सुन्दर सुखवाली स्त्रियां मै श्रेष्ठ जनकतनया से बोले

3.sa: सुमन्त्रस्त्वपि शत्रुघ्नमदूरादन्वपद्यत।रामदर्शनजस्तर्षो भरतस्येव तस्य च ॥ २.९९.३॥
3.en: Sumantra, who was overeager, like Bharata, to see Rama, followed Satrughna who was not far from him.
3.hi: हे वैदेही ! इस विचित्र तटं वाली, रमणीय और हंस सारसादि पत्तियों से सेवित मन्दाकिनी नदी को देखो

4.sa: गच्छन्नेवाथ भरतस्तापसालयसंस्थिताम्।भ्रातु: पर्णकुटीं श्रीमानुटजं च ददर्श ह ॥ २.९९.४॥
4.en: While walking, Bharata beheld a hut made of leaves looking like a hermit's cottage.
4.hi: इस नदी के उभय तट फल फूल वाले अनेक जाति के वृर्छो से परिपूर्ण हैं । उनसे इस नदी की शोभा वैसी ही हो रही है जैसी कि कुवेर की सौगन्धिका नाम्नी नदी की

5.sa: शालायास्त्वग्रतस्तस्या ददर्श भरतस्तदा।काष्ठानि चावभग्नानि पुष्पाण्युपचितानि च ॥ २.९९.५॥
5.en: In front of that hut Bharata beheld shattered logs of wood and also flowers plucked.
5.hi: इस नदी के सव घाट'बड़े रमणीय हैं । अतः वहाँ जा कर स्नान करने की मेरी इच्छा हो रही हे । अभी मृगो के फुड इन घाटों पर जल पी कर गए हैं। अतः वहाँ का जल गँदला हो रहा है

6.sa: सलक्ष्मणस्य रामस्य ददर्शाश्रममीयुष:।कृतं वृक्षेष्वभिज्ञानं कुशचीरै: क्वचित् क्वचित् ॥ २.९९.६॥
6.en: Bharata beheld here and there knots of kusa grass and strips of bark tied on trees as signs to ascertain the way to the hermitage of Rama and Lakshmana.
6.hi: हे प्रिये ! देखो, जटा और मृगचर्म धारण किए और वृक्षों की छाल पहिने हुए ऋषि लोग, इस नदी में यथासमय स्नान करते हैँ

7.sa: ददर्श च वने तस्मिन् महत: सञ्चयान् कृतान्।मृगाणां महिषाणां च कऺरीषै: शीतकारणात् ॥ २.९९.७॥
7.en: He also beheld large heaps of dried cakes of dung of buffaloes and deer for use against cold in the forest.
7.hi: हे विशालाक्षि ! इस ओर ये सब तीक्षण नियमों का पालन करने वाले मुनिगण नियमानुसार ऊपर को बाँह उठा कर सूर्य अगवान का उपस्थान कर रहे हें

8.sa: गच्छन्नेव महाबाहुर्द्युतिमान् भरतस्तदा।शत्रुघ्नं चाब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तानमात्यांश्च सर्वश: ॥ २.९९.८॥
8.en: Walking on, the longarmed, effulgent and delighted Bharata said to Satrughna and the ministers surrounding him:
8.hi: देखो पवन से कम्पित इन वृक्षा के हिलने से यह पत्र'त eS तव्रताः-तीच्णनियमाः । ( गो० ) ५ मारुतोद्ध,त शिखरै:--वायु- कम्पितशाखैः । ( गो० ) | पुष्प गिरते हैँ उनसे चित्रकूट पर्वत मानों नदी को पुष्पाञ्जलि रहा है

9.sa: मन्ये प्राप्ता: स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्।नातिदूरे हि मन्येऽहं नदीं मन्दाकिनीमित: ॥ २.९९.९॥
9.en: We must have reached the region about which Bharadwaja had spoken. I think river Mandakini is not far from here.

10.sa: उच्चैर्बद्धानि चीराणि लक्ष्मणेन भवेदयम्।अभिज्ञानकृत: पन्था विकाले गन्तुमिच्छता ॥ २.९९.१०॥
10.en: Here are long bark garments fastened on lofty places as marks of identification left by Lakshmana, to locate the path at odd times which may be needed while going out.
10.hi: हे भद्रे ! वायु के मोकों में नदी के तट पर हट हुए पुष्पों के हेर को देखो । जो फूल जल में उड़ कर जा गिरे हैं, वे पानी पर कैसे उतरा रहे हैं, उन्हें भी तुम देखो

11.sa: इदं चोदात्तदन्तानां कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्।शैलपार्श्वे परिक्रान्तमन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम् ॥ २.९९.११॥
11.en: This must be the place on the hillside on which mighty tuskers wander about trumpeting and charging at one another.
11.hi: हे कल्याणि ! फूलों के ढेरों पर चढ़े हुए चक्रवाक्र रति के लिए अपनी मादाओं को बुलाने के हेतु कैसी मधुर बोली बोल रहे हैं

12.sa: यमेवाधातुमिच्छन्ति तापसा: सततं वने।तस्यासौ दृश्यते धूम: सङ्कुल: कृष्णवर्त्मन: ॥ २.९९.१२॥
12.en: Here is the thick smoke emanating from the blacktrailed fire maintained perpetually by the ascetics living in the forest.

13.sa: अत्राहं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गुरुसंस्कारकारिणम्।आर्यं द्रक्ष्यामि संहृष्टो महर्षिमिव राघवम् ॥ २.९९.१३॥
13.en: I shall see here with a delighted heart the venerable Rama, the best of men, who renders great hospitality (to elders) and who resembles a maharshi.
13.hi: हे सीते ! अब तुम इस मन्दाकिनी नदी में, जिसमें शम, दम और तप से यक्त एवं पापरहित लिद्रलोग नित्य स्नान किआ करते हैं, चल कर मेरे साथ स्नान करो

14.sa: अथ गत्वा मुहूर्तं तु चित्रकूटं स राघव:।मन्दाकिनीमनुप्राप्तस्तं जनं चेदमब्रवीत् ॥ २.९९.१४॥
14.en: Bharata walked for a short distance towards mount Chitrkuta when he reached river Mandakini. And then said to his ministers:
14.hi: हे सीते ! तुम जैसे अपनी सखियों के साथ निःशङ्क जलक्रीड़ा करतीं थीं, वैसे ही मेरे साथ भी इस मंदाकिनी में लाल सफेद कसल के फूलों को डुवोती हुई जलक्रीडा करो

15.sa: जगत्यां पुरुषव्याघ्र आस्ते वीरासने रत:।जनेन्द्रो निर्जनं प्राप्य धिङ्मे जन्म सजीवितम् ॥ २.९९.१५॥
15.en: Rama, the lord of men, a tiger among men, is sitting on the ground in a 'heroic' (yogic) posture in this secluded forest. O fie upon my birth and my life
15.hi: टिप्पणी--लाल सफेद कमल के फूलों से भूषणटीकाकार ने यह अभिप्राय बतलाया है-- स्तनजघनाघातजनिततरद्धे रितिभावः किन्तु शिरोमणिटीकाकार का कथन है कि, क्रीड़ा के लिए लाल सफेद रंग के कमलों से मंदाकिनी के जल को ढक दो | त्वं पौरजनवद्‌“द्वयालानयोध्यामिव पर्वतम्‌ | मन्यस्व वनिते नित्यं सरयूवदिमां नदीस्‌

16.sa: मत्कृते व्यसनं प्राप्तो लोकनाथो महाद्युति:।सर्वान् कामान् परित्यज्य वने वसति राघव: ॥ २.९९.१६॥
16.en: Effulgent Rama, the lord of the world, had to renounce all desires and undergo this calamity of living in the forest on my account.
16.hi: हे वैदेही ! यह धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मण मेरे आज्ञाकारी हैं और तुम भी सदा मेरी आज्ञा के अनुसार काम किया करती हो । इससे सुके बड़ी प्रसन्नता होती है

17.sa: इति लोकसमाक्रुष्ट: पादेष्वद्य प्रसादयन्।रामस्य निपतिष्यामि सीताया लक्ष्मणस्य च ॥ २.९९.१७॥
17.en: Reviled by the world, I shall now fall at the feet of Sita, Rama and Lakshmana seeking their grace.
17.hi: त्रिकाल स्नान और तुम्हारे ' साथ मधु मूल और फल का ` भोजन करता हुआ, मैं, अयोध्या के बास की और राज्य की आकांक्षा नहीं करता

18.sa: एवं स विलपंस्तस्मिन् वने दशरथात्मज:।ददर्श महतीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम् ॥ २.९९.१८॥
18.en: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.
18.hi: जो गर्जो के यूथों से युक्त है और जिसका जल हाथी, सिंह ओर बंदर पिया करते हैं, उस रमणीय एव सुन्दर पुष्पां से यक्त वृक्षों द्वारा शोभित मंदाकिनी नदी का सेवन कर, वह कौन पुरुष है जो दुःखी से छट, सुखी न हो ?

19.sa: सालतालाश्वकर्णानां पर्णैर्बहुभिरावृताम्।विशालां मृदुभिस्तीर्णां कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे ॥ २.९९.१९॥
19.en: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

20.sa: शक्रायुधनिकाशैश्च कार्मुकैर्भारसाधनै:।रुक्मपृष्टष्ठैर्महासारै: शोभितां शत्रुबाधकै: ॥ २.९९.२०॥
20.en: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

21.sa: अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशैर्घोरैस्तूणीगतै: शरै:।शोभितां दीप्तवदनै: सर्प्पैर्भोगवतीमिव ॥ २.९९.२१॥
21.en: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

22.sa: महारजतवासोभ्यामसिभ्यां च विराजिताम्।रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्यां चर्मभ्यां चापि शोभिताम् ॥ २.९९.२२॥
22.en: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

23.sa: गोधाङ्गुलित्रैरासक्तैश्चित्रै: काञ्चनभूषितै:।अरिसङ्घैरनाधृष्यां मृगै: सिंहगुहामिव ॥ २.९९.२३॥
23.en: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

24.sa: प्रागुदक्प्रवणां वेदिं विशालां दीप्तपावकाम्।ददर्श भरतस्तत्र पुण्यां रामनिवेशने ॥ २.९९.२४॥
24.en: Bharata beheld at Rama's residence a sacred and spacious altar sloping to the northeast, with a burning fire upon it.

25.sa: निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्त्तं तु ददर्श भरतो गुरम्।उटजे राममासीनं जटामण्डलधारिणम् ॥ २.९९.२५॥
25.en: Bharata looked around for a moment and saw his esteemed brother Rama seated in that thatched cottage wearing matted locks of hair.

26.sa: तं तु कृष्णाजिनधरं चीरवल्कलवाससम्।ददर्श राममासीनमभित: पावकोपमम् ॥ २.९९.२६॥
26.en: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

27.sa: सिंहस्कन्धं महाबाहुं पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम्।पृथिव्या: सागरान्ताया भर्त्तारं धर्मचारिणम् ॥ २.९९.२७॥
27.en: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

28.sa: उपविष्टं महाबाहुं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्।स्थण्डिले दर्भसंस्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च ॥ २.९९.२८॥
28.en: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

29.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा भरत: श्रीमान् दु:खशोकपरिप्लुत:।अभ्यधावत धर्मात्मा भरत: कैकयीसुत: ॥ २.९९.२९॥
29.en: Beholding Rama, Bharata the majestic and righteous son of Kaikeyi overwhelmed with grief and distress rushed towards him.

30.sa: दृष्ट्वैव विललापार्त्तो बाष्पसन्दिग्धया गिरा।अशक्नुवन् धारयितुं धैर्याद्वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ २.९९.३०॥
30.en: On seeing Rama, Bharata could not control his grief with patience and lamented in great anguish and with words choked with tears said:

31.sa: य: संसदि प्रकृतिभिर्भवेद्युक्त उपासितुम्।वन्यैर्मृगैरुपासीन: सोऽयमास्ते ममाग्रज: ॥ २.९९.३१॥
31.en: My elder brother who deserves to be attended by ministers and other subjects in the royal assembly sits here today in the forest surrounded by wild beasts.

32.sa: वासोभिर्बहुसाहस्रैर्यो महात्मा पुरोचित:।मृगाजिने सोऽयमिह प्रवस्ते धर्ममाचरन् ॥ २.९९.३२॥
32.en: Such magnanimous Rama, a follower of dharma, accustomed to be attired in thousands of dresses in the past now clad in two deer skins, is practising righteousness.

33.sa: अधारयद्यो विविधाश्चित्रा: सुमनसस्तदा सोऽयं जटाभारमिमं वहते राघव: कथम् ॥ २.९९.३३॥
33.en: How is it that Rama who used to wear variegated flowers formerly, now bears these heavy matted locks?

34.sa: यस्य यज्ञैर्यथोद्दिष्टैर्युक्तो धर्मस्य सञ्चय:।शरीरक्लेशसम्भूतं स धर्मं परिमार्गते ॥ २.९९.३४॥
34.en: That Rama, who in accordance with tradition deserves accredition of religious merit through sacrifices now seeks it through mortification of body.

35.sa: चन्दनेन महार्हेण यस्याङ्गमुपसेवितम्।मलेन तस्याङ्गमिदं कथमार्यस्य सेव्यते ॥ २.९९.३५॥
35.en: How is it that the body of my venerable brother which was once smeared with expensive, fragrant sandal paste is now covered with dust?

36.sa: मन्निमित्तमिदं दु:खं प्राप्तो राम: सुखोचित:।धिग्जीवितं नृशंसस्य मम लोकविगर्हितम् ॥ २.९९.३६॥
36.en: It is on my account that Rama who was accustomed to all comforts has fallen into this misfortune. Fie on my life of cruelty which is condemned by the world.

37.sa: इत्येवं विलपन् दीन: प्रस्विन्नमुखपङ्कज:।पादावप्राप्य रामस्य पपात भरतो रुदन् ॥ २.९९.३७॥
37.en: Thus Bharata lamented in misery and with his lotuslike countenanace sweating before reaching Rama's feet fell down, crying in distress.

38.sa: दु:खाभितप्तो भरतो राजपुत्रो महाबल:।उक्त्वार्येति सकृद्दीनं पुनर्नोवाच किञ्चन ॥ २.९९.३८॥
38.en: Mighty prince Bharata, oppressed with grief, could only say, O Arya (venerable one) And in distress could not speak any more.

39.sa: बाष्पापिहितकण्ठश्च प्रेक्ष्य रामं यशस्विनम्।आर्येत्येवाथ संक्रुश्य व्याहर्त्तुं नाशकत्तदा ॥ २.९९.३९॥
39.en: As he beheld the glorious Rama, with his throat choken with tears, he cried out, O Arya (venerable one) and thereafter, was unable to speak any more.

40.sa: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि रामस्य ववन्दे चरणौ रुदन्।तावुभौ स समालिङ्ग्य रामश्चाश्रूण्यवर्त्तयत् ॥ २.९९.४०॥
40.en: Satrughna also prostrated himself at the feet of tearful Rama who embraced both of them.

41.sa: तत: सुमन्त्रेण गुहेन चैव समीयतू राजसुतावरण्ये।दिवाकरश्चैव निशाकरश्च यथाम्बरे शुक्रबृहस्पतिभ्याम् ॥ २.९९.४१॥
41.en: Thereafter, princes Rama and Lakshmana joined Sumantra and Guha in the forest like the Sun and the Moon meeting the planets Sukra and Brihaspati in the sky.

42.sa: तान् पार्थिवान् वारणयूथपाभान् समागतांस्तत्र महत्यरण्ये।वनौकसस्तेऽपि समीक्ष्य सर्वेप्यश्रूण्यमुञ्चन् प्रविहाय हर्षम् ॥ २.९९.४२ ॥
42.en: On seeing the princes now assembled in the great forest like mighty leaders of elephant herds, inhabitants of the forest had nothing but tears of grief, not joy, to shed. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyninth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

1.sa: जटिलं चीरवसनं प्राञ्जलिं पतितं भुवि ।ददर्श रामो दुर्दर्शं युगान्ते भास्करं यथा ॥ २.१००.१॥
1.en: Rama beheld Bharata with matted locks and robes of bark fallen down on the ground with folded hands like the Sun at the time of dissolution of the world. It was really difficult to look at him.

2.sa: कथञ्चिदभिविज्ञाय विवर्णवदनं कृशम् ।भ्रातरं भरतं राम: परिजग्राह बाहुना ॥ २.१००.२॥
2.en: Rama found it extremely difficult to recognise Bharata with his emaciated body and pallid face. He held him in his arms and lifted him.
2.hi: श्रीरामचन्द्र जी ने सीता से कहा-देखो, यह मांस पवित्र है ओर अभ्नि में भूजने से यह स्वादिष्ट हो गया है श्रीरामचन्द्र जी सीलासहित वहाँ बैठे हुए बातंचीत कर रहे थे कि,

3.sa: आघ्राय रामस्तं मूर्ध्नि परिष्वज्य च राघव: ।अङ्के भरतमारोप्य पर्यपृच्छत् समाहितः ॥ २.१००.३॥
3.en: Born in the race of Raghu, Rama embraced Bharata and kissed him on his forehead. Placing him on his lap, he enquired thus with a composed mind:
3.hi: इतने में उनके पास आती हुई अरत जी की सेना के चलने से उड़ो हुई आकाश को छती हुई धूल देख पड़ी ओर कोलाहल सुनाई दिआ

4.sa: क्व नु ते ऽभूत् पिता तात यदरण्यं त्वमागत: ।न हि त्वं जीवतस्तस्य वनमागन्तुमर्हसि ॥ २.१००.४॥
4.en: O dear, now that you have come to the forest, where is our father king Dasaratha? You ought not come to the forest while he is living.
4.hi: उस महाकोलाहल से त्रस्त हो, बड़े बड़े यूथपति गजेन्द्र विकल हो अपने अपने यूथों को ले इधर उधर भागने लगे

5.sa: चिरस्य बत पश्यामि दूराद्भरतमागतम् ।दुष्प्रतीकमरण्ये ऽस्मिन् किं तात वनमागत: ॥ २.१००.५॥
5.en: You have come a long distance (from Ayodhya) to this forest, O Bharata It is a pity, dear brother, to see you after a long time, so emaciated. What brings you to the forest?

6.sa: कच्चिद्धारयते तात राजा यत्त्वमिहागत: ।कच्चिन्न दीन: सहसा राजा लोकान्तरं गत: ॥ २.१००.६॥
6.en: My dear (brother), now that you have come here, I trust, king Dasaratha is keeping good health and hope, he has not departed prematurely in despondency for the other world.
6.hi: उन हाथियों को भागते देख और सेना का कोलाहल सुन श्रीरामचन्द्र जी ने तेजस्वी लक्ष्मण से कहा

7.sa: कच्चित् सौम्य न ते राज्यं भ्रष्टं बालस्य शाश्वतम् ॥ २.१००.७॥
7.en: O gentle one, being young and inexperienced, I trust, you have not forfeited the kingdom for ever. Dear child, I trust, you are looking after father whose prowess is his truthfulness.
7.hi: हे लक्ष्मण ! तुमसे पुत्र को पा कर सुमित्रा देवी सुपुत्रवती है । देखो तो, यह भयङ्कर बादल की गड्गड़ाहट जैसे गम्भीर एवं तुमुल शब्द कहाँ सुन पड़ता दै

8.sa: कच्चिच्छुश्रूषसे तात पितरं सत्यविक्रमम् ॥ २.१००.८॥
8.en: I trust king Dasaratha, who is true to his promise, a performer of Rajasuya and Ashwamedha sacrifices and a firm adherent of righteousness is in good health.
8.hi: जिसको सुन, सघन वनवासी हाथियों के झु ड, जंगली मैंसे ओर मृगों के झु ड सिंहों सहित भयभीत हो बड़ी तेजी से इधर उधर भाग रहे हें

9.sa: कच्चिद्दशरथो राजा कुशली सत्यसङ्गर: ।राजसूयाश्वमेधानामाहर्त्ता धर्मनिश्चय: ॥ २.१००.९॥
9.en: O dear child I trust, the family preceptor of the Ikshvakus, Vasistha, the brahmin (versed in the Vedas), who is learned, ever fixed in virtues and effulgent is being honoured as usual.

10.sa: स कच्चिद् ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् धर्मनित्यो महाद्युति: ।इक्ष्वाकूणामुपाध्यायो यथावत्तात पूज्यते ॥ २.१००.१०॥
10.en: Dear child I trust, Kausalya and Sumitra, mothers of an excellent progeny are happy. I trust, the noble queen Kaikeyi is happy too.
10.hi: हे लक्ष्मण ! इस रदद पर अब पक्षी भी तो भली माँति नहीं घूम सकते । अतएव तुम. शीघ्र इस बात का ठीक ठीक पता. लगाओ

11.sa: सा तात कच्चित्कौसल्या सुमित्रा च प्रजावती ।सुखिनी कच्चिदार्य्या च देवी नन्दति कैकयी ॥ २.१००.११॥
11.en: I trust, you continue to honour the family priest (Suyajna, son of Vasistha) who is endowed with modesty, born of high family, conversant in scriptures, free from envy and who can give you directions with regard to your duties.
11.hi: श्रीरामचन्द्र जी का ऐसा वचन सुन लक्ष्मण जी तुरन्त एक फूले हुए साल बृत्ष पर चढ़ गए और चारों ओर देखते हुए उन्होंने प्रथम पूव दिशा की ओर देखा

12.sa: कच्चिद्विनयसम्पन्न: कुलपुत्रो बहुश्रुत: ।अनसूयुरनुद्रष्टा सत्कृतस्ते पुरोहित: ॥ २.१००.१२॥
12.en: I trust, the sagacious priest who knows ritual precepts, who is upright and is employed to take care of your sacred fires, informs you always regarding what was offered and what is to be offered as oblation at appropriate time.

13.sa: कच्चिदग्निषु ते युक्तो विधिज्ञो मतिमानृजु: ।हुतं च होष्यमाणं च काले वेदयते सदा ॥ २.१००.१३॥
13.en: Dear brother, I trust you continue to pay homage to gods, father, mothers, teachers, relations equal to your father, aged people, physicians and brahmins.
13.hi: हाथियों घोड़ों से युक्त, रथ की पताकाओं से भूषित, उस सेना का वृत्तान्त निवेदन करते हुए, लद््रण्‌ जी ने श्रीरामचन्द्र जी से कहा

14.sa: कच्चिद्देवान् पितऽन् मातऽर्गुरून् पितृसमानपि ।वृद्धांश्च तत वैद्यांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चाभिमन्यसे ॥ २.१००.१४॥
14.en: I hope you treat with respect Sudhanva who is equipped with the most formidable arrows and other weapons propelled by mantras and a master in the science of statecraft.
14.hi: यह्‌ सुन पुरुषसिह्‌ श्रोरामचन्द्र जो ने लक्ष्मण जी से कहा, हे वत्स सौमित्र ! ध्वज चिह्णों को देख यह वो निश्चय करो कि यह सेना है किसकी ?

15.sa: इष्वस्त्रवरसम्पन्नमर्थशास्त्रविशारदम् ।सुधन्वानमुपाध्यायं कच्चित्त्वं तात मन्यसे ॥ २.१००.१५॥
15.en: I hope, dear brother, you have appointed men who are brave, learned, selfcontrolled, of noble birth and skilled in guessing from hints.

16.sa: कच्चिदात्मसमा: शूरा: श्रुतवन्तो जितेन्द्रिया: ।कुलीनाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च कृतास्ते तात मन्त्रिण: ॥ २.१००.१६॥
16.en: O Bharata the wellguarded advice of ministers, learned in scriptures and capable of proper counselling, is the root of victory for kings, specially when the advice is kept in confidence.
16.hi: श्रीरामचन्द्र जी के ऐसे वचन सुन, लक्ष्मण जी क्रोध के : मारे अग्नि के समान हो, उस सेना को मानों भस्म कर डालने के लिए यह बोले,

17.sa: मन्त्रो विजयमूलं हि राज्ञां भवति राघव ।सुसंवृतो मन्त्रधरैरमात्यै: शास्त्रकोविदै: ॥ २.१००.१७॥
17.en: I trust you are not under the grip of sleep but wake up at appropriate times, I hope you always think of the means of judicious statecraft during the last part of the night.
17.hi: साफ देख पड़ता है कि, केकेयी का पुत्र भरते राज्याभिषेक पा कर भी, अकण्टक राज्य करने की कामना से, हम दोनों का वध करने के लिए आ रहा है

18.sa: कच्चिन्निद्रावशं नैषी: कच्चित्काले प्रबुध्यसे ।कच्चिच्चापररात्रेषु चिन्तयस्यर्थनैपुणम् ॥ २.१००.१८॥
18.en: I hope you neither decide alone nor discuss with many. I trust a decision once made by you is not leaked in the kingdom.
18.hi: देखिए, वह जो बड़ा और खूब हराभरा सुन्दर बृ देख पड़ता है, उसके पास जो रथ है, उस पर कचनार वृक्ष के आकार की ध्वजा फहरा रही है

19.sa: कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैक: कच्चिन्न बहुभि: सह ।कच्चित्ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति ॥ २.१००.१९॥
19.en: O Bharata, having determined on an endeavour involving a little effort and yielding great results, I trust you commence to execute it quickly without procrastination?

20.sa: कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं महोदयम् ।क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्त्तुं न दीर्घयसि राघव ॥ २.१००.२०॥
20.en: I trust, other kings come to know of your endeavours only when your endeavours suceed or about to succeed. I hope, efforts intended to be made in future are not revealed to them beforehand.
20.hi: अत्र हे वीर ! हम दोनों धनुष बाण ले इस पवत पर चढ़ चलें अथवा दोनों जन, कवच पाहून और हथियार णे यहीं खड़े हो जांय

21.sa: कच्चित्ते सुकृतान्येव कृतरूपाणि वा पुन: ।विदुस्ते सर्वकार्याणि न कर्त्तव्यानि पार्थिवा: ॥ २.१००.२१॥
21.en: Dear brother, I hope others are not able to understand your determination or those of your ministers, either by conjecture or by inference or through other means without being revealed either by you or by your ministers.
21.hi: कोविदार ध्वजा वाले भरत को निश्चय ही हम लोग युद्ध में अपने वश में कर लेंगे । भरत केकारण ही तो यह विपत्ति आई हे । आज हम उसे समझ लेंगे

22.sa: कच्चिन्न तर्कैर्युक्त्या वा ये चाप्यपरिकीर्तिता: ।त्वया वा वा ऽमात्यैर्बुध्यते तात मन्त्रितम् ॥ २.१००.२२॥
22.en: I hope by setting aside a thousand fools, you prefer a single wise man. A wise man will be of immense help in difficult situations.
22.hi: हे रघुनन्दन ! जिसके लिए तुम्हें, मुझे और सीता को इस ` दुदशा में पड़ना पड़ा है ओर जितके कारण तुम सनातन राज्य च्युत किए गए हो

23.sa: कच्चित् सहस्रान् मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम् ।पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु कुर्य्यान्नि:श्रेयसं महत् ॥ २.१००.२३॥
23.en: Even if the king seeks the assistance from thousands or tens of thousands of fools, they cannot render any help to him.

24.sa: सहस्राण्यपि मूर्खाणां यद्युपास्ते महीपति: ।अथवाप्ययुतान्येव नास्ति तेषु सहायता ॥ २.१००.२४॥
24.en: A single clearsighted minister who is prudent, brave and skilful can bring about great prosperity to a king or a prince.
24.hi: क्योंकि पूव अपकारी को मार. डालने में कुछ भी पाप नहीं लगता । हे राबव ! यह भरत पूर्व में अपकार कर चुका है । अतः इसको मार डालने ही में पुण्य है

25.sa: एकोप्यमात्यो मेधावी शूरो दक्षो विचक्षण: ।राजानं राजमात्रं वा प्रापयेन्महतीं श्रियम् ॥ २.१००.२५॥
25.en: I hope you have employed highly competent servants for important tasks, mediocre servants in mediocre tasks and low people in inferior tasks.
25.hi: इसको मार कर आप सम्पूण प्रथिवी के राज्य का उप- भोग कीजिए । आज वह केकेयी जो राज्य पाने की कामना किए हुए है अपने पुत्र को युद्ध में मरा हुआ दखेगी

26.sa: कच्चिन्मुख्या महत्स्वेव मध्यमेषु च मध्यमा: ।जघन्यास्तु जघन्येषु भृत्या: कर्मसु योजिता: ॥ २.१००.२६॥
26.en: I hope you are assigning ministers, who are unyielding to bribery and other temptations, holding positions hereditarily and who are full of integrity and eminence, with superior tasks.
26.hi: हाथी के तोड़े हुए वृक्ष की तरह मेरे हाथ से भरत को मरा हुआ दुख, केकेयी अत्यन्त दुःखित होगी । मैं उस केकेयो को भी उसके भाबईन्दों और मंथरादि सहित मार डाल गा

27.sa: अमात्यानुपधातीतान् पितृपैतामहाञ्छुचीन् ।श्रेष्ठान् श्रेष्ठेषु कच्चित्त्वं नियोजयसि कर्मसु ॥ २.१००.२७॥
27.en: Are not the citizens of your kingdom agitated at severe punishment meted out to them reproaching your ministers?
27.hi: जिससे कि यह प्रथिवी उस केकेयी रूपी महापाप से छुट- कारा पा ज्ञाय । ह मान के देने वाले ! आज बहुत दिनों के रोके हुए क्रोध को और कैकेयी के किए हुए तिरस्कार को

28.sa: कच्चिन्नोग्रेण दण्डेन भृशमुद्वेजितप्रजम् ।राष्ट्रं तवानुजानन्ति मन्त्रिण: कैकयीसुत ॥ २.१००.२८॥
28.en: Just like a performer of sacrifice scorns at an outcaste or a woman scorns at a lustful lover, do the subjects not scorn you for collecting taxes more than what is due?
28.hi: शत्र की सेना के ऊपर वैसे ही छोडूंगा जैसे सुखे णो के डेर पर आग छोड़ी जाती है। आज ही सैं चित्रकूट के बन को अपने तीखे बाणां से

29.sa: कच्चित्त्वां नावजानन्ति याजका: पतितं यथा ।उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारं कामयानमिव स्त्रिय: ॥ २.१००.२९॥
29.en: A learned person but skilled in contrivances, a warrior with passion for wealth and a man ever engaged in corrupting the minds of servants must be slain. A king who does not kill them is himself killed in due course.

30.sa: उपायकुशलं वैद्यं भृत्यसन्दूषणे रतम् ।शूरमैश्वर्यकामं च यो न हन्ति स वध्यते ॥ २.१००.३०॥
30.en: I trust you have appointed a man who is cheerful, brave, sagacious, steadfast, honest, of a good family, loyal and efficient as the army chief.
30.hi: इति षण्णवतितमः सगः ॥ भ्राज सैं इस महासंग्राम में सेनासहित भरत का बध कर अपने धनुष और बाणों के ऋण से निस्सन्देंह उऋण हो जाऊगा

31.sa: कच्चिद्धृष्टश्च शूरश्च मतिमान् धृतिमाञ्छुचि: ।कुलीनश्चानुरक्तश्च दक्ष: सेनापति: कृत: ॥ २.१००.३१॥
31.en: I trust you honour and respect those prominent soldiers who are courageous, powerful, skilled in war and who have proven heroic exploits.

32.sa: बलवन्तश्च कच्चित्ते मुख्या युद्धविशारदा: ।दृष्टापदाना विक्रान्तास्त्वया सत्कृत्य मानिता: ॥ २.१००.३२॥
32.en: I trust you distribute rations and wages to your army in due time without making delay.

33.sa: कच्चिद्बलस्य भक्तं च वेतनं च यथोचितम् ।सम्प्राप्तकालं दातव्यं ददासि न विलम्बसे ॥ २.१००.३३॥
33.en: It has been mentioned in the scriptures that if provisions and wages are not paid in stipulated time, the dependent attendants will be incensed with their masters and will turn hostile and become corrupt, leading to great calamity.

34.sa: कालातिक्रमणाच्चैव भक्तवेतनयोर्भृता: ।भर्त्तु: कुप्यन्ति दुष्यन्ति सो ऽनर्थ: सुमहान् स्मृत: ॥ २.१००.३४॥
34.en: I hope all men of a good family, especially those who belong to our race, are loyal to you and are ready to sacrifice their lives for your cause.

35.sa: कच्चित् सर्वे ऽनुरक्तास्त्वां कुलपुत्रा: प्रधानत: ।कच्चित्प्राणांस्तवार्थेषु सन्त्यजन्ति समाहिता: ॥ २.१००.३५॥
35.en: O Bharata, I hope you have chosen as your envoy an expert born in your own country, wellinformed, skilful and quick to understand one who repeats and reports (exactly) what has been told.

36.sa: कच्चिज्जानपदो विद्वान् दक्षिण: प्रतिभानवान् ।यथोक्तवादी दूतस्ते कृतो भरत पण्डित: ॥ २.१००.३६॥
36.en: I hope you collect information (of their secret efforts) intelligently through unrecognisable spies with three of them closely watching each of the eighteen officials (there are eighteen categories of officials in a kingdom) of the enemy's side and fifteen (officials) on your side.

37.sa: कच्चिदष्टादशान्येषु स्वपक्षे दश पञ्च च ।त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरविज्ञातैर्वेत्सि तीर्थानि चारकै: ॥ २.१००.३७॥
37.en: O slayer of foes, I hope you are always alert about your foes who were defeated by you and have come back. You should not ignore your enemies thinking they are weak.

38.sa: कच्चिद्व्यपास्तानहितान् प्रतियातांश्च सर्वदा ।दुर्बलाननवज्ञाय वर्त्तसे रिपुसूदन ॥ २.१००.३८॥
38.en: Dear brother, I hope you do not serve those brahmins who are atheists, who foolishly think of this world alone and fancy themselves as learned. They only bring disasters.

39.sa: कच्चिन्न लोकायतिकान् ब्राह्मणांस्तात सेवसे ।अनर्थकुशला ह्येते बाला: पण्डितमानिन: ॥ २.१००.३९॥
39.en: While principal scriptures do exist, these superficial fellows take resort to the science of logic based on abstract reasoning, and indulge in futile talks.

40.sa: धर्मशास्त्रेषु मुख्येषु विद्यमानेषु दुर्बुधा: ।बुद्धिमान्वीक्षिकीं प्राप्य निरर्थं प्रवदन्ति ते ॥ २.१००.४०॥
40.en: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

41.sa: वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकै: ।सत्यनामां दृढद्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम् ॥ २.१००.४१॥
41.en: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

42.sa: ब्राह्मणै: क्षत्ऺित्रयैर्वैश्यै: स्वकर्मनिरतै: सदा ।जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै: सहस्रश: ॥ २.१००.४२॥
42.en: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

43.sa: प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम् ।कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि ॥ २.१००.४३॥
43.en: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

44.sa: कच्चिच्चित्यशतैर्जुष्ट: सुनिविष्टजनाकुल: ।देवस्थानै: प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभित: ॥ २.१००.४४॥
44.en: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

45.sa: प्रहृष्टनरनारीक: समाजोत्सवशोभित: ।सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान् हिंसाभि: परिवर्जित: ॥ २.१००.४५॥
45.en: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

46.sa: अदेवमातृको रम्य: श्वापदै: परिवर्जित: ।परित्यक्तो भयै: सर्वै: खनिभिश्चोपशोभित: ॥ २.१००.४६॥
46.en: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

47.sa: विवर्जितो नरै: पापैर्मम पूर्वै: सुरक्षित: ।कच्चिज्जनपद: स्फीत: सुखं वसति राघव ॥ २.१००.४७॥
47.en: I trust all those men who live on agriculture and cattlerearing are favourable to you. The world's prosperity, dear brother, grows on the profession of cattle rearing.

48.sa: कच्चित्ते दयिता: सर्वे कृषिगोरक्षजीविन: ।वार्त्तायां संश्रितस्तात लोको हि सुखमेधते ॥ २.१००.४८॥
48.en: I trust you nourish them and also afford portection and prevent adversities. A king must protect all those people living in his country in accordanc with righteousness.

49.sa: तेषां गुप्तिपरीहारै: कच्चित्ते भरणं कृतम् ।रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिन: ॥ २.१००.४९॥
49.en: I trust, you keep the women pacified and wellprotected, you do not believe their words and do not divulge any secrets to them.

50.sa: कच्चित् स्त्रिय: सान्त्वयसि कच्चित्ताश्च सुरक्षिता: ।कच्चिन्न श्रद्दधास्यासां कच्चिद् गुह्यं न भाषसे ॥ २.१००.५०॥
50.en: I trust, you protect the habitat of elephants and you have a large number of milch cows. I trust you are not contented with the existing number of female and male elephants and horses.

51.sa: कच्चिन्नागवनं गुप्तं कच्चित्ते सन्ति धेनुका: ।कच्चिन्न गणिकाश्वानां कुञ्जराणां च तृप्यसि ॥ २.१००.५१॥
51.en: O prince, I trust, you rise early daily and present yourself welladomed to the people on the thoroughfare.

52.sa: कच्चिद्दर्शयसे नित्यं मनुष्याणां विभूषितम् ।उत्थायोत्थाय पूर्वाह्णे राजपुत्र महापथे ॥ २.१००.५२॥
52.en: All the servants, I trust, do not present themselves to you directly. At the same time they do not remain out of sight with fear at a distance. The middle course is the best way for the welfare of every one.

53.sa: कच्चिन्न सर्वे कर्मान्ता: प्रत्यक्षास्ते ऽविशङ्कया ।सर्वे वा पुनरुत्सृष्टा मध्यमेवात्र कारणम् ॥ २.१००.५३॥
53.en: Hope all the forts are adequately provided with wealth, foodgrains, weapons and water, with machines of war and craftsmen and archers.

54.sa: कच्चित् सर्वाणि दुर्गाणि धनधान्यायुधोदकै: ।यन्त्रैश्च परिपूर्णानि तथा शिल्पिधनुर्द्धरै ॥ २.१००.५४॥
54.en: O Bharata, I trust, your revenues are abundant and expenditure much less. I trust you do not give away your treasure to undeserving persons.

55.sa: आयस्ते विपुल: कच्चित् कच्चिदल्पतरो व्यय: ।अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित्कोशो गच्छति राघव ॥ २.१००.५५॥
55.en: I trust, you are spending only on gods, ancestors, brahmins, guests, warriors and hosts of friends.

56.sa: देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थे ब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु च ।योधेषु मित्रवर्गेषु कच्चिद्गच्छति ते व्यय: ॥ २.१००.५६॥
56.en: I trust a man who is honest, purehearted and venerable, falsely accused of adultery is not slain out of avarice without consulting experts in scriptures.

57.sa: कच्चिदार्य्यो विशुद्धात्मा ऽ ऽक्षारितश्चोरकर्मणा ।अपृष्ट: शास्त्रकुशलैर्न लोभाद्वध्यते शुचि: ॥ २.१००.५७॥
57.en: O best among men I trust that a thief, caught redhanded and interrogated and has sufficient proof is not set free, out of greed for money.

58.sa: गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्ट: सकारण: ।कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ ॥ २.१००.५८॥
58.en: O Bharata, I trust that your ministers are wellinformed and look into all matters in times of hardship pertaining to whether a man is rich or poor without any bias to either.

59.sa: व्यसने कच्चिदाढ्यस्य दुर्गतस्य च राघव ।अर्थं विरागा: पश्यन्ति तवामात्या बहुश्रुता: ॥ २.१००.५९॥
59.en: O Bharata, the tears falling from the eyes of persons, who are falsely accused and punished for the pleasure of the king will destroy his progeny and cattle as well.

60.sa: यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यस्राणि राघव ।तानि पुत्रपशून् घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासत: ॥ २.१००.६०॥
60.en: O Bharata, I trust you wish to thrive by treating the old, children and foremost of learned people with the three expedients namely gifts, affection and kind words.

61.sa: कच्चिद् वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च वैद्यमुख्यांश्च राघव ।दानेन मनसा वाचा त्रिभिरेतैर्बुभूषसे ॥ २.१००.६१॥
61.en: I trust you pay homage to the preceptors, the aged ones, ascetics, gods and guests, to shrines and to accomplished brahmins.

62.sa: कच्चिद्गुरूंश्च वृद्धांश्च तापसान् देवतातिथीन् ।चैत्यांश्च सर्वान् सिद्धार्थान् ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यसि ॥ २.१००.६२॥
62.en: I trust, righteousness for the sake of prosperity or prosperity for the sake of righteousness or both for the sake of sensual pleasure are not thwarted by you.

63.sa: कच्चिदर्थेन वा धर्ममर्थं धर्मेण वा पुन: ।उभौ वा प्रीतिलोभेन कामेन च न बाधसे ॥ २.१००.६३॥
63.en: O Bharata, the best among the victorious, conversant with timely actions and a bestower of boons you are the best of men. I trust, you allocate adequate time for attending to all the three expedients of life like dharma, artha and kama.

64.sa: कच्चिदर्थं च धर्मं च कामं च जयतां वर ।विभज्य काले कालज्ञ सर्वान् वरद सेवसे ॥ २.१००.६४॥
64.en: O highly sagacious Bharata, those brahmins who can comprehend the meaning of all scriptures along with the inhabitants of the city and country, I trust, are seeking your happiness.

65.sa: कच्चित्ते ब्राह्मणा: शर्म सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदा: ।आशंसन्ते महाप्राज्ञ पौरजानपदै: सह ॥ २.१००.६५॥
65.en: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

66.sa: नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम् ।अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम् ॥ २.१००.६६॥
66.en: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

67.en: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

68.sa: मङ्गलस्याप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वत: ।कच्चित्त्वं वर्जयस्येतान् राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश ॥ २.१००.६८॥
68.en: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

69.sa: दश पञ्च चतुर्वर्गान् सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वत: ।अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव ॥ २.१००.६९॥
69.en: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

70.sa: इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्वा षाङ्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम् ।कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गञ्च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम् ॥ २.१००.७०॥
70.en: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

71.en: I trust you deliberate in secrecy on your counsel with three or four counsellors, together and separately with each one, as laid down in sacred texts.

72.sa: मन्त्रिभिस्त्वं यथोद्दिष्टैश्चतुर्भिस्त्रिभिरेव वा ।कच्चित् समस्तैर्व्यस्तैश्च मन्त्र मन्त्रयसे मिथ: ॥ २.१००.७२॥
72.en: I trust, the Vedas you have studied are fruitful, the acts which you commenced are productive, your wife is fruitful (blessed with a son) and the scriptures you studied are useful.

73.sa: कच्चित्ते सफला वेदा: कच्चित्ते सफला: क्रिया: ।कच्चित्ते सफला दारा: कच्चित्ते सफलं श्रुतम् ॥ २.१००.७३॥
73.en: O Bharata, I trust your intellect is in conformity with what I said conducive to long life, and fame in accordance with righteousness, (legitimate) pleasure and prosperity.

74.sa: कच्चिदेषैव ते बुद्धिर्यथोक्ता मम राघव ।आयुष्या च यशस्या च धर्मकामार्थसंहिता ॥ २.१००.७४॥
74.en: I trust, you walk the auspicious path of truth (virtue) followed by our father and forefathers.

75.sa: यां वृत्तिं वर्त्तते तातो यां च न: प्रपितामहा: ।तां वृत्तिं वर्त्तसे कच्चिद्या च सत्पथगा शुभा ॥ २.१००.७५॥
75.en: O Bharata, I trust you do not partake delicious food all by yourself, and you share it with your friends when they want it.

76.sa: कच्चित् स्वादु कृतं भोज्यमेको नाश्नासि राघव ।कच्चिदाशंसमानेभ्यो मित्रेभ्य: सम्प्रयच्छसि ॥ २.१००.७६॥
76.en: The highly sagacious and learned king, having acquired the entire earth and punishing the people in accordance with tradition and righteously ruling the kingdom, will ascend the his release (from this world). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे शततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

1.sa: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरत: प्रत्युवाच ह ।किं मे धर्माद्विहीनस्य राजधर्म: करिष्यति ॥ २.१०१.१॥
1.en: On listening to Rama, Bharata replied Of what use shall be these royal duties to me, when I have fallen from righteousness?

2.sa: शाश्वतो ऽयं सदा धर्म्म: स्थितो ऽस्मासु नरर्षभ ।ज्येष्ठपुत्रे स्थिते राजन्न कनीयान् नृपो भवेत् ॥ २.१०१.२॥
2.en: O best of men there is an ancient tradition in our race that the younger son cannot become king when the eldest is there.
2.hi: हे लक्ष्मण ! बड़ा धनुष धारण करने वाले और बड़े पण्डित भरत जव स्त्रयं आए हैं, तव उनके सामने तुम्हारे धनुष और ढाल तलवार की जरूरत ही क्या है? (अर्थात उनसे तुम जीत नहीं सकते )

3.sa: स समृद्धां मया सार्द्धमयोध्यां गच्छ राघव ।अभिषेचय चात्मानं कुलस्यास्य भवाय न: ॥ २.१०१.३॥
3.en: Therefore, O scion of the Raghu race, return along with me to prosperous Ayodhya and for the good of our race get your self coronated.

4.sa: राजानं मानुषं प्राहुर्देवत्वे स मतो मम ।यस्य धर्मार्थसहितं वृत्तमाहुरमानुषम् ॥ २.१०१.४॥
4.en: Other think the king to be a human, but to me, he is divine since his conduct and the statecraft are superhuman as they are in conformity with righteousness.
4.hi: जो धन, बन्धुत्रान्धरों और इष्टमित्रो का वध करने से ग्राप्त हो, उसे सैं तो ग्रहण नहीं कर सकता । क्योंकि झैं तो उसे विष मिले हुए भोजन की तरह त्याज्य समता हूँ

5.sa: केकयस्थे च मयि तु त्वयि चारण्यमाश्रिते ।दिवमार्यो गतो राजा यायजूक: सतां मत: ॥ २.१०१.५॥
5.en: While I was in Kekaya and you took refuge in the forest, venerable king (Dasaratha), who was always engaged in sacrifices and was held in high esteem by the virtuous, ascended to heaven.
5.hi: हे लक्ष्मण ! सैं तुमसे यह बात दावे के साथ कहता हूँ कि, मैं तो केवल अपने भाइयों ही के लिए धर्म, अर्थ, काम अथवा प्रथिवी का राज्य चाहता हूँ

6.sa: निष्क्रान्तमात्रे भवति सहसीते सलक्ष्मणे ।दु:खशोकाभिभूतस्तु राजा त्रिदिवमभ्यगात् ॥ २.१०१.६॥
6.en: As soon as you set out for the forest along with Sita and Lakshmana, the king, overwhelmed with grief, attained heaven.
6.hi: हे लक्ष्मण ! मैं सत्य सत्य अपने हथियारों को छ कर, तुमसे कहता हूँ कि, मैं जो राज्य की कामना करता हूँ वह अपने भाइयों के पालन और सुख के लिए ही करता हूँ

7.sa: उत्तिष्ठ पुरुषव्याघ्र क्रियतामुदकं पितु: ।ऺअहं चायं च शत्रुघ्न: पूर्वमेव कृतोदकौ ॥ २.१०१.७॥
7.en: Arise, O best of men and offer libations to our father. I and Satrughna have already done so.
7.hi: हे सौम्य ! ससागरा प्रथिवी का राज्य हस्तगत करना मेरै लिए.दुलेभ नहीं, प्रथिवी तो है ही क्या? मैं अधमंपूबक तो इन्द्रपद्‌ को भी लेना नहीं चाहता

8.sa: प्रियेण खलु दत्तं हि पितृलोकेषु राघव ।अक्षय्यं भवतीत्याहुर्भवांश्चैव पितु: प्रिय: ॥ २.१०१.८॥
8.en: O son of Raghu's race, it is said that whatever is offered by a dear son becomes eternal in the world of manes. You alone are the beloved son of our father.

9.sa: त्वामेव शोचंस्तव दर्शनेप्सुस्त्वय्येव सक्तामनिवर्त्य बुद्धिम् ।त्वया विहीनस्तव शोकरुग्णस्त्वां संस्मरन्नस्तमित: पिता ते ॥ २.१०१.९ ॥
9.en: Your father, deprived of you, brooding over you, wishing to behold you, unable to divert his mind fixed on you, remembering you alone and immersed in sorrow departed (from this world). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोत्तर शततम स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredone sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

12.hi: बहुत सम्भव है कि) अम्मा कैकेयी के अपर क्रुद्ध हो ओर उसको कुछ कठोर वचन कह तथा पिता को मना कर मुझे मनाने को वह आया हो

13.hi: यह उचित ही है कि, भरत आ कर हमसे मिले, परन्तु यह सम्भव नहीं कि भरत हमारे अनिष्ट की कसी कल्पना भीः करे

14.hi: क्या भरत ने उससे पूर्व कभो तुम्हारा कुछ अहत किआ था जो तुम उसकी ओर से भय की शङ्का कर रह हो

15.hi: भरत के विषय में ऐसे कठोर और अप्रिय वचन तुन्हे न्‌ कहना चाहिए क्योंकि भरत क वारे में जो कुछ तुम खरी खाटी बातें कहोगे या उसका कुछ अहित करोगे ता मानों बह तुमने मुभीसे कठोर वचन कहें और मेरा हीईअहित किआ

16.hi: हे लक्ष्मण ! जरा सोचो तो | चाहे केसी भारी विपत्ति क्यो न आन पड़े पिता किसी भी दशा में अपने पुत्र का या आई प्राण के समान अपने भाई का वप नहीं कर सकता

1.sa: तां श्रुत्वा करुणां वाचं पितुर्मरणसंहिताम् ।राघवो भरतेनोक्तां बभूव गतचेतन: ॥ २.१०२.१॥
1.en: Having heard the words of Bharata regarding the death of his father, Rama became unconscious.
1.hi: अयोध्याकाण्ड का सत्तानवेवाँ सग समाप्त हुआ । . +#- | अष्टनवतितमः सगः निवेश्य सेनां तु विश्व) पड़यां पादवतांर वरः । अभिगन्त्‌ स काङुर्स्थमियेष शरुवतिनम्‌ २६

2.sa: तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा ।वाग्वज्रं भरतेनोक्तममनोज्ञं परन्तप: ॥ २.१०२.२॥
2.en: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.
2.hi: भरत जी फे आज्ञानुसार जब सेना ठहर गई तत्र भरत जी ने शत्र॒घ्र से कहा,

3.sa: प्रगृह्य बाहू रामो वै पुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुम: ।वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह ॥ २.१०२.३॥
3.en: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

4.sa: तथा निपतितं रामं जगत्यां जगतीपतिम् ।कूलघातपरिश्रान्तं प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम् ॥ २.१०२.४॥
4.en: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

5.sa: भ्रातरस्ते महेष्वासं सर्वत: शोककर्शितम् ।रुदन्त: सह वैदेह्या सिषिचु: सलिलेन वै ॥ २.१०२.५॥
5.en: Those brothers on all sides, with Sita lamenting, sprinkled water on Rama, the great archer and lord of the earth who, afflicted with grief, had fallen down on the ground, and was lying like an elephant exhausted from repeatedly striking a river bank.
5.hi: बोलने वालों में श्रेष्ठ महात्मा.भरत जी पव त के शिखरों पर लगे हुए फूले फले वृक्षा के बीच में जा पहुँचे

6.sa: स तु संज्ञां पुनर्लब्ध्वा नेत्राभ्यामास्रमुत्सृजन् ।उपाक्रामत काकुत्स्थ: कृपणं बहु भाषितुम् ॥ २.१०२.६॥
6.en: On regaining consciousness, shedding tears profusely, Rama again started speaking piteously.
6.hi: यावन्न राज्ये राज्याहः पिठपैतामहे स्थितः अभिपेकजलकिल्न्नो न मे शान्तिभत्रिष्यति ॥ & ॥ जब तक राज्य करने योग्य राम के उस पितृपितामह के राज्य पर अभिषेक के जल से आद्र ( भींगे न होंगे, तब तक सेरा जी ठिकाने न होगा

7.sa: स राम: स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा पितरं पृथिवीपतिम् ।उवाच भरतं वाक्यं धर्मात्मा धर्मसंहितम् ॥ २.१०२.७॥
7.en: On hearing that his father, king Dasaratha, the lord of the world had attained heaven, righteous Rama said to Bharata in conformty with his rightful conduct.

8.sa: किं करिष्याम्ययोध्यायां ताते दिष्टां गतिं गते ।कस्तां राजवराद्धीनामयोध्यां पालयिष्यति ॥ २.१०२.८॥
8.en: What shall I do in Ayodhya now that my father has followed the path ordained by the gods? Who will rule that Ayodhya deprived of that best of kings?
8.hi: जब सक मैं भाई के राजचिहों से युक्त चरणयुगल अपने मस्तक पर धारण न कर लूँगा, तब तक मेरा मन शान्त न होगा

9.sa: किं नु तस्य मया कार्य्यं दुर्जातेन महात्मन: ।यो मृतो मम शोकेन मया चापि न संस्कृत: ॥ २.१०२.९॥
9.en: I could not even perform the last rites of that magnanimous one who died of grief on account of me. What use is my life with an unlucky birth?

10.sa: अहो भरत सिद्धार्थो येन राजा त्वया ऽनघ ।शत्रुघ्नेन च सर्वेषु प्रेतकृत्येषु सत्कृत: ॥ २.१०२.१०॥
10.en: O irreproachable Bharata, it is gratifying that you and Satrughna are indeed fortunate to have fulfilled your cherished desire since the king was wellhonoured by you with all the obsequial rites.
10.hi: सिद्धाथः खलु सौमित्रियश्चन्द्रविमलोपमम्‌ । सुखं पश्यति रामस्य राजीवाक्षे महाद्यति १० ॥ धन्य है लक्ष्मण, जो राम के उस निर्मल चम्द्रोपम मह।द्यति युक्त एव कमल सश नेत्र वाले मुख को, देखा करता है

11.sa: निष्प्रधानामनेकाग्रां नरेन्द्रेण विना कृताम् ।निवृत्तवनवासोपि नायोध्यां गन्तुमुत्सहे ॥ २.१०२.११॥
11.en: Even after the completion of my exile I do not wish to return to Ayodhya which is directionless, bereft of its chief, the king.

12.sa: समाप्तवनवासं मामयोध्यायां परन्तप ।को नु शासिष्यति पुनस्ताते लोकान्तरं गते ॥ २.१०२.१२॥
12.en: O subduer of enemies, when father has gone to the other world, who will guide me in Ayodhya after I complete my term of exile?
12.hi: हिमालय पव त के समान यह चित्रकूट पवत भी धन्य हे । क्योंकि इस पर राम उसी प्रकार वास करते हैं, जिस प्रकार कुवेर चैत्ररथ वन सें

13.sa: पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन् ।वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुत: कर्णसुखान्यहम् ॥ २.१०२.१३॥
13.en: On seeing my good conduct our father used to say comforting words to me. Now from whom can I hear such words pleasing to the ears?
13.hi: यह्‌ बन जो सर्पो से भरा होने के कारण, दुर्गम है, कृतार्थ हुआ क्योंकि इसमें शस्र चलाने वालों में भ्रष्ठ, राम रहते हुँ

14.sa: एवमुक्त्वा स भरतं भार्यामभ्येत्य राघव: ।उवाच शोकसन्तप्त: पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् ॥ २.१०२.१४॥
14.en: Having thus spoken to Bharata, Rama, overwhelmed with grief, approached his wife Sita whose face looked like the full Moon, and said to her.
14.hi: तब तो भरत जी अपने बान्धवों सहित हर्षित हुए और यहीं रहते इँ--यह निश्चय कर, मानौं सुदर के पार हो गए

15.sa: सीते मृतस्ते श्वशुर: पित्रा हीनो ऽसि लक्ष्मण ।भरतो दु:खमाचष्टे स्वर्गतं पृथिवीपतिम् ॥ २.१०२.१५॥
15.en: O Sita, your fatherinlaw is dead. O Lakshmana, you are deprived of your father. Bharata is relating to me the sad news that king Dasaratha has attained his heavenly abode.

16.sa: ततो बहुगुणं तेषां बाष्पं नेत्रेष्वजायत ।तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे कुमाराणां यशस्विनाम् ॥ २.१०२.१६॥
16.en: While the scion of the Kakutsthas was saying thus, copious tears welled up from the eyes of all those illustrious sons of Dasaratha.
16.hi: भरत ने वहाँ एक साखू के वृक्ष के ऊपर लड़ कर श्रीराम चन्दे के आश्रम में जलती हुई अग्नि का बहुत ऊंचा उठता हुआ छुझओं देखा

17.sa: ततस्ते भ्रातर: सर्वे भृशमाश्वास्य राघवम् ।अब्रुवन् जगतीभर्त्तु: क्रियतामुदकं पितु: ॥ २.१०२.१७॥
17.en: All the brothers, having consoled Rama as best they could, told him, Let the libations be offered to our father, the protector of the world.

18.sa: सा सीता श्वशुरं श्रुत्वा स्वर्गलोकगतं नृपम् ।नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यामशकन्नेक्षितुं पतिम् ॥ २.१०२.१८॥
18.en: On hearing that her fatherinlaw, king Dasaratha, had attained heaven, Sita, her eyes filled with tears could not look at her husband in the face.

19.sa: सान्त्वयित्वा तु तां रामो रुदन्तीं जनकात्मजाम् ।उवाच लक्ष्मणं तत्र दु:खितो दु:खितं वच: ॥ २.१०२.१९॥
19.en: Having consoled Sita, daughter of Janaka, griefstricken Rama said to Lakshmana who was also distressed with grief.

20.sa: आनयेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं चीरमाहर चोत्तरम् ।जलक्रियार्थं तातस्य गमिष्यामि महात्मन: ॥ २.१०२.२०॥
20.en: I shall go and offer libations to my magnanimous father. Go and fetch the dried pulp of ingudi fruit and an upper garment made of bark.

21.sa: सीता पुरस्ताद्व्रजतुत्वमेनामभितो व्रज ।अहं पश्चाद्गमिष्यामि गतिर्ह्येषा सुदारुणा ॥ २.१०२.२१॥
21.en: Let us proceed in this order -- you first, Sita second and I last. This procession in mourning is terrible indeed.

22.sa: ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामति: ।मृदुर्दान्तश्च शान्तश्च रामे च दृढभक्तिमान् ॥ २.१०२.२२॥
22.en: Thereafter, their constant follower Sumantra who was conversant in spiritual knowledge, a highminded person, softnatured, selfcontrolled, tranquilminded and staunchly devoted to Rama consoled him. Holding the hands of the princes, Sumantra helped their descent into the auspicious river Mandakini for taking bath.

23.sa: सुमन्त्रस्तैर्नृपसुतै: सार्द्धमाश्वास्य राघवम् ।अवातारयदालम्ब्य नदीं मन्दाकिनीं शिवाम् ॥ २.१०२.२३॥
23.en: Thereafter, their constant follower Sumantra who was conversant in spiritual knowledge, a highminded person, softnatured, selfcontrolled, tranquilminded and staunchly devoted to Rama consoled him. Holding the hands of the princes, Sumantra helped their descent into the auspicious river Mandakini for taking bath.

24.sa: ते सुतीर्थां तत: कृच्छ्रादुपागम्य यशस्विन: ।नदीं मन्दाकिनीं रम्यां सदा पुष्पितकाननाम् ॥ २.१०२.२४॥
24.en: The illustrious brothers approached with great difficulty the swiftflowing and enchanting river Mandakini which had convenient descent and endowed with forests always in bloom. They descended at an auspicious place that was not slushy and offered libations of water saying 'O father, let these offerings be yours'.

25.sa: शीघ्रस्रोतसमासाद्य तीर्थं शिवमकर्द्दमम् ।सिषिचुस्तूदकं राज्ञे तत्रैतत्ते भवत्विति ॥ २.१०२.२५॥
25.en: The illustrious brothers approached with great difficulty the swiftflowing and enchanting river Mandakini which had convenient descent and endowed with forests always in bloom. They descended at an auspicious place that was not slushy and offered libations of water saying 'O father, let these offerings be yours'.

26.sa: प्रगृह्य च महीपालो जलपूरितमञ्जलिम् ।दिशं याम्यामभिमुखो रुदन् वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ २.१०२.२६॥
26.en: Rama, the ruler of the earth, held water with both palms cupped and, facing the south, the direction of Yama (the god of death) said these words, sobbing:

27.sa: एतत्ते राजशार्दूल विमलं तोयमक्षयम् ।पितृलोकगतस्याद्य मद्दत्तमुपतिष्ठतु ॥ २.१०२.२७॥
27.en: 'O best of kings, you are gone to the world of the manes, and let this inexhaustible libation of pure water reach you'.

28.sa: ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरात् प्रत्युत्तीर्य्य स राघव: ।पितुश्चकार तेजस्वी निवापं भ्रातृभि: सह ॥ २.१०२.२८॥
28.en: Then, the powerful scion of the Raghu race reached bank, from the bathing spot of the river Mandakini along with his brothers and offered pinda (an offering of rice flour to the departed) to his late lamented father.

29.sa: ऐङ्गुदं बदरीमिश्रं पिण्याकं दर्भसंस्तरे ।न्यस्य राम: सुदु:खार्त्तो रुदन् वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ २.१०२.२९॥
29.en: Placing the balls of ingudi pulp mixed with badari fruit on a spread of darbha grass, Rama, was overcome with grief and weeping, said:

30.sa: इदं भुङ्क्ष्व महाराज प्रीतो यदशना वयम् ।यदन्न: पुरुषो भवति तदन्नास्तस्य देवता: ॥ २.१०२.३०॥
30.en: O great king, we offer you such food as we partake now. Be pleased to accept it. For, his gods are offered the food a man takes.

31.sa: ततस्तेनैव मार्गेण प्रत्युत्तीर्य्य नदीतटात् ।आरुरोह नरव्याघ्रो रम्यसानुं महीधरम् ॥ २.१०२.३१॥
31.en: Rama, the tiger among men, ascending the riverbank and proceeding on the same path (he had come), climbed the (Chitrakuta) mountain of charming slopes.

32.sa: तत: पर्णकुटीद्वारमासाद्य जगतीपति: ।परिजग्राह बाहुभ्यामुभौ भरतलक्ष्मणौ ॥ २.१०२.३२॥
32.en: Rama, lord of the earth, reached the door of the leafhut and took Bharata and Lakshmana in his arms.

33.sa: तेषां तु रुदतां शब्दात् प्रतिश्रुत्को ऽभवद्गिरौ ।भ्रातऽणां सह वैदेह्या: सिंहानामिव नर्दताम् ॥ २.१०२.३३॥
33.en: The mountain echoed with the sound of lamentations of all the brothers along with Sita which resembled the roar of lions.

34.sa: महाबलानां रुदतां कुर्वतामुदकं पितु: ।विज्ञाय तुमुलं शब्दं त्रस्ता भरतसैनिका: ॥ २.१०२.३४॥
34.en: The soldiers of Bharata were alarmed on hearing the tumultuous sounds raised by those mighty brothers offering libations of water and lamenting.

35.sa: अब्रुवंश्चापि रामेण भरत: सङ्गतो ध्रुवम् ।तेषामेव महाञ्छब्द: शोचतां पितरं मृतम् ॥ २.१०२.३५॥
35.en: They said, 'Bharata must have joined Rama. That loud noise must be their wailing over their deceased father'.

36.sa: अथ वासान् परित्यज्य तं सर्वे ऽभिमुखा: स्वनम् ।अप्येकमनसो जग्मुर्यथास्थानं प्रधाविता: ॥ २.१०२.३६॥
36.en: Then all of them left their camps with one single thought (of seeing Rama) in their minds and ran in the direction from where that sound emanated.

37.sa: हयैरन्ये गजैरन्ये रथैरन्ये स्वलङ्कृतै: ।सुकुमारास्तथैवान्ये पद्भिरेव नरा ययु: ॥ २.१०२.३७॥
37.en: Some rode horses, some, elephants, while others mounted welldecorated chariots, while the young went on foot.

38.sa: अचिरप्रोषितं रामं चिरविप्रोषितं यथा ।द्रष्टुकामो जन: सर्वो जगाम सहसाश्रमम् ॥ २.१०२.३८॥
38.en: The whole multitude of people at once rushed towards the hermitage wishing to see Rama as if he had left long ago though he had gone on exile very recently.

39.sa: भ्रातऽणां त्वरितास्तत्र द्रष्टुकामा: समागमम् ।ययुर्बहुविधैर्यानै: खुरनेमिस्वनाकुलै: ॥ २.१०२.३९॥
39.en: Eager to see the union of brothers, all those people went by every sort of vehicle filled with the sounds of hooves and wheels.

40.sa: सा भूमिर्बहुभिर्यानै: खुरनेमिसमाहता ।मुमोच तुमुलं शब्दं द्यौरिवाभ्रसमागमे ॥ २.१०२.४०॥
40.en: The earth crushed by several vehicles, hooves (of horses) and wheels (of chariots) emitted tumultuous sounds like the sky in the gathering stormclouds.

41.sa: तेन वित्रासिता नागा: करेणुपरिवारिता: ।आवासयन्तो गन्धेन जग्मुरन्यद्वनं तत: ॥ २.१०२.४१॥
41.en: Frightened by the sound, the elephants followed by their females, spreading all the way the odour of the ichor, moved to other forests.

42.sa: वराहवृकसङ्घाश्च महिषा: सर्प्पवानरा: ।व्याघ्रगोकर्णगवया: वित्रेसु: पृषतैः सह ॥ २.१०२.४२॥
42.en: Hearing that sound, hosts of boars and deer, buffaloes, serpents and apes, tigers, antelopes with ears like the cows', gavayas as well as dappled antelopes were all frightened.

43.sa: रथाङ्गसाह्वा नत्यूहा: हंसा: कारण्डवा: प्लवा: ।तथा पुंस्कोकिला: क्रौञ्चा विसंज्ञा भेजिरे दिश: ॥ २.१०२.४३॥
43.en: Ducks, watercranes, geese, karandavas, cranes, male cuckoos and kraunchas fled senselessly in different directions.

44.sa: तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तैराकाशं पक्षिभिर्वृतम् ।मनुष्यैरावृता भूमिरुभयं प्रबभौ तदा ॥ २.१०२.४४॥
44.en: The sky was filled with birds frightened by the sound and the earth covered with people. Both looked extremely beautiful.

45.sa: ततस्तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं यशस्विनमरिन्दमम् ।आसीनं स्थण्डिले रामं ददर्श सहसा जन: ॥ २.१०२.४५॥
45.en: All at once the people saw the illustrious Rama, the best of men, and the subduer of enemies squatting on the bare earth.

46.sa: विगर्हमाण: कैकेयीं सहितो मन्थरामपि ।अभिगम्य जनो रामं बाष्पपूर्णमुखो ऽभवत् ॥ २.१०२.४६॥
46.en: All those men with faces full of tears, reproaching Kaikeyi and Manthara (all the way), approached Rama.

47.sa: तान्नरान् बाष्पपूर्णाक्षान् समीक्ष्याथ सुदु:खितान् ।पर्य्यष्वजत धर्मज्ञ: पितृवन्मातृवच्च स: ॥ २.१०२.४७॥
47.en: Thereafter, beholding those people deeply afflicted, their eyes full of tears, Rama embraced them as if they were his own father and mother.

48.sa: स तत्र कांच्चित् परिषस्वजे नरान्नराश्च केचित्तु तमभ्यवादयन् ।चकार सर्वान् सवयस्य बान्धवान् यथार्हमासाद्य तदा नृपात्मज: ॥ २.१०२.४८॥
48.en: Rama embraced some, while others paid him obeisance. Therafter, he honoured his erstwhile companions and relations in accordance with their status.

49.sa: स तत्र तेषां रुदतां महात्मनां भुवं च खं चानुनिनादयन् स्वन: ।गुहा गिरीणां च दिशश्च सन्ततं मृदङ्गघोषप्रतिम: प्रशुश्रुवे ॥ २.१०२.४९ ॥
49.en: The weeping and the tumult of those magnanimous people made the earth, sky, mountaincaves and all quarters reverberate incessantly like the beating of drums. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे द्व्युत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundred and second sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

1.sa: वसिष्ठ: पुरत: कृत्वा दारान् दशरथस्य च ।अभिचक्राम तं देशं रामदर्शनतर्षित: ॥ २.१०३.१॥
1.en: Longing to see Rama, Vasistha, headed by the wives of Dasaratha, set out on foot (where Rama was offering libations).

2.sa: राजपत्न्यश्च गच्छन्त्यो मन्दं मन्दाकिनीं प्रति ।ददृशुस्तत्र तत्तीर्थं रामलक्ष्मणसेवितम् ॥ २.१०३.२॥
2.en: The wives of the king while proceeding slowly towards the river Mandakini beheld the bathing place frequented by Rama and Lakshmana.
2.hi: भरत ने वसिष्ठ जी से कहा कि आप मेरी माताओं को शीघ्र छे आइए, ( मैं आगे चलता हूँ ) यह कह गुरुवत्सल. भरते शीघ्रता से आगे चले

3.sa: कौसल्या बाष्पपूर्णेन मुखेन परिशुष्यता ।सुमित्रामब्रवीद्दीना याश्ऺचान्या राजयोषित: ॥ २.१०३.३॥
3.en: Kausalya, with eyes filled with tears and her face emaciated, addressing Sumitra and the other wives of the king sadly said:
3.hi: इतने में सुमंत्र भी शत्रुत्न को भरत के प्रीछे जाते देख, स्वयं शत्रन के पीछे हो लिए । क्योंकि भरत की तरह सुमंत्र को भी राम के दशन की उत्कण्टा थी

4.sa: इदं तेषामनाथानां क्लिष्टमक्लिष्टकर्मणाम् ।वने प्राक्केवलं तीर्थं ये ते निर्विषयीकृता: ॥ २.१०३.४॥
4.en: This is a sacred place to the east of the forest used by the unfortunate Rama, and Lakshmana of untiring energy and Sita expelled from the country and undergoing suffering.
4.hi: भरत जी ने जाते जाते देखा कि, तपस्वियां के आश्रमा के बीच भाई की पर्णकुटी बनी हुई है

5.sa: इत: सुमित्रे पुत्रस्ते सदा जलमतन्द्रित: ।स्वयं हरति सौमित्रिर्मम पुत्रस्य कारणात् ॥ २.१०३.५॥
5.en: O Sumitra, your son Lakshmana, free from laziness, always carries water from here for the sake of my son.

6.sa: जघन्यमपि ते पुत्र: कृतवान्न तु गर्हित: ।भ्रातुर्यदर्थसहितं सर्वं तद्विहितं गुणै: ॥ २.१०३.६॥
6.en: Your son, though engaged in servile tasks (like bringing water), is not to be held contemptible because all the services intended for the benefit of his brother are prompted by virtue.
6.hi: काष्ठानि-- रात्रौप्रकाशायज्वलनीयानि । ( गोऽ ) २ पुष्पारिण पूजार्थानि | ( गो० ) ६४८ योध्याकाण भरत जी ने यह भी देखा कि, उम पण शाला के सामने ही (रात में प्रकाश करने के लिए) टूटी लकड़ियाँ और पूजन के लिए फूल चुन चुन कर रखे हुए हैँ ॥ «॥ सलच्मणस्य रामस्य ददर्शाश्रममीयुषः । कृतं वक्षेप्यभिज्ञानं कुशचीरेः कचित्क्कचिद्‌

7.sa: अद्यायमपि ते पुत्र: क्लेशानामतथोचित: ।नीचानर्थसमाचारं सज्जं कर्म प्रमुञ्चतु ॥ २.१०३.७॥
7.en: This your son unaccustomed to, and undeserving of, any suffering may now give up this mean and distressing duty entrusted to him.
7.hi: भरत जी ने देखा कि, शीत से बचने के लिए अथवा तापने के लिथे, मृगां और“में तो के गोवर के सूखे' कंडों का ढेर लगा हैं

8.sa: दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु सा ददर्श महीतले ।पितुरिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं न्यस्तमायतलोचना ॥ २.१०३.८॥
8.en: That largeeyed Kausalya beheld the cakes of ingudi pulp placed by Rama for his father on a spread of darbha grass whose blades pointed toward the south.
8.hi: मन्ये प्राप्ताः स्म त देश भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्‌ । नातिदरे हि मन्येऽहं नदीं मन्दाकिनीमितः | & ॥ : महात्राहु घृतिवान्‌ भरत जी ने चत्तते चलते प्रसन्न हो अपने सब मंत्रियों और शत्र॒न्न से कहा--जान पड़ता है, हम ,लोग उस स्थान पर पहुँच गए हैं जिसे भरद्वान जी ने बतलाया था। मैं समता हुँ कि, यहाँ से मन्दाकिनी नदी भी समीप ही है

9.sa: तं भूमौ पितुरार्तेन न्यस्तं रामेण वीक्ष्य सा ।उवाच देवी कौसल्या सर्वा दशरथस्त्रिय: ॥ २.१०३.९॥
9.en: Seeing the pinda (edible offering made to the departed soul) placed on the ground for his father by the distressed Rama, queen Kausalya, addressing all the wives of Dasaratha, said:

10.sa: इदमिक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य राघवस्य महात्मन: ।राघवेण पितुर्दत्तं पश्यतैतद्यथाविधि ॥ २.१०३.१०॥
10.en: Have darsan of this pinda offered by Rama according to tradition to his magnanimous father, Dasaratha, lord of the Ikshvaku race.
10.hi: यहाँ इतनी ऊँचाई पर लक्ष्मण ने चोरों को बाँधा है । यह इस लिए कि, रातत्रिरात में जत्र लक्ष्मण को पानी लाने के लिए जाना पड़ता होगा, तत्र इन चीरचिहों को देख, वे आश्रम भें | बिना इधर उधर भटके आ जाते होंगे

11.sa: तस्य देवसमानस्य पार्थिवस्य महात्मन: ।नैतदौपयिकं मन्ये भुक्तभोगस्य भोजनम् ॥ २.१०३.११॥
11.en: I do not think that this is an appropriate food for that godlike and great lord of the earth who enjoyed all luxury.

12.sa: चतुरन्तां महीं भुक्त्वा महेन्द्रसदृशो विभु: ।कथमिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं स भुङ्क्ते वसुधाधिप: ॥ २.१०३.१२॥
12.en: How can Indralike Dasaratha, having ruled the earth bounded by four oceans, eat a cake of ingudi pulp?
12.hi: वेगवान एवं बड़े वडे दाँतों वाले हाथी जो बड़ा नाद किआ करते हैं, पवत क पास यह उन्हींके आने जाने का रास्ता जान पड़ता है. ॥ ?१ ॥ . यमेत्राधातुमिच्छान्ति तापसाः सततं वने । तस्यासौ इश्यते धूमः सङ्कलः कृष्णवत्मनः

13.sa: अतो दु:खतरं लोके न किञ्चित् प्रतिभाति मा ।यत्र राम: पितुर्दद्यादिङ्गुदीक्षोदमृद्धिमान् ॥ २.१०३.१३॥
13.en: Rama (who was once) highly prosperous, had to offer the cake of ingudi pulp to his father. Nothing appears more painful to me than this in this world.
13.hi: अतः इसी स्थान पर उस पुरुपलिह एव श्रेष्ठ संस्कार करने वाले श्रीराम को, एक हषयुक महर्षि के समान बैठा हुआ, मैं देखूंगा

14.sa: रामेणेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं पितुर्दत्तं समीक्ष्य मे ।कथं दु:खेन हृदयं न स्फोटति सहस्रधा ॥ २.१०३.१४॥
14.en: Seeing the offering of cake of ingudi pulp by Rama to his father, how is it that my heart does not break into a thousand pieces in sorrow?
14.hi: देखो वह पुरुषसिंह और नरेन्द्र हो कर भूमि पर बीरासन हो हैं और इस निजनस्थान में रहते हैं । हा ! मेरे जोवन ओर जन्म को धिक्कार हे

15.sa: श्रुतिस्तु खल्वियं सत्या लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा ।यदन्न: पुरुषो भवति तदन्नास्तस्य देवता: ॥ २.१०३.१५॥
15.en: The wellknown saying in this world is that 'whatever food a man partakes, his gods also partake the same'. This dictum appears true (now).

16.sa: एवमार्त्तां सपत्न्यस्ता जग्मुराश्वास्य तां तदा ।ददृशुश्चाश्रमे रामं स्वर्गच्युतमिवामरम् ॥ २.१०३.१६॥
16.en: The cowives, having thus consoled the distressed Kausalya, went to the hermitage. There they beheld Rama who looked like a god dislodged from heaven.
16.hi: हा ! मेरे हो पीछे, सब के स्वामी और महाद्युतिमान्‌ राम दारुण दुरवस्था में पढ़े हे आर सत्र प्रकार के सुखभोगो से वब्चित हो, वन में वाउ करे हें

17.sa: सर्वभोगै: परित्यक्तं रामं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मातर: ।आर्त्ता मुमुचुरश्रूणि सस्वरं शोककर्शिता: ॥ २.१०३.१७॥
17.en: Beholding Rama devoid of all luxury, his mothers afflicted with grief, and overcome with sorrow, cried aloud, tears streaming down.

18.sa: तासां राम: समुत्थाय जग्राह चरणान् शुभान् ।मातऽणां मनुजव्याघ्र: सर्वासां सत्यसङ्गर: ॥ २.१०३.१८॥
18.en: Rama, the best among men and true to his promise, rose and touched the auspicious feet of all his mothers (in reverence).
18.hi: इससे सेरी सब में बडो बदनामी हुई है ( अतः उस बदनामी को दूर करने के लिए ) मैं बार वार राम और सीता के चरणों पर गिर, उसको प्रसन्न करू गा ।! १७॥। १ तजन --सहागत शात्रुघ्नादिकम्‌ । ( गो०) २ जगत्यां--भूमो | ( गो० ) # पाठान्तरे--“सीदाया लक्ष्मणस्य |” एवं स विलपंस्तस्मिन्‌ बने दशरथात्मजः | ददश सहता पुण्या पणशाला मनोरमाम्‌

19.sa: ता: पाणिभि: सुखस्पर्शैर्मृद्वङ्गुलितलै: शुभै: ।प्रममार्जू रज: पृष्ठाद्रामस्यायतलोचना: ॥ २.१०३.१९॥
19.en: Those largeeyed queens, their palms with delicate fingers and with auspicious hands with a pleasant touch, wiped the dust from the back of his body.

20.sa: सौमित्रिरपि ता: सर्वा: मातऽ: सम्प्रेक्ष्य दु:खित: ।अभ्यवादयतासक्तं शनै रामादनन्तरम् ॥ २.१०३.२०॥
20.en: On seeing his mothers, Lakshmana, too, was overcome with grief and with devotion followed Rama and slowly bowed to them with reverence.
20.hi: उसे जहाँ तहाँ, इन्द्र क वञ्ज क समान, युद्ध में बड़े बड़े काम करने वाले और सुत्रणरचित पीठ ब्राले, बड़े भारी भारी तथा शत्रु को बाधा देने वाले धनुष, टगे हुए शोभायमान हो रहे थे

21.sa: यथा रामे तथा तस्मिन् सर्वा ववृतिरे स्त्रिय: ।वृत्तिं दशरथाज्जाते लक्ष्मणे शुभलक्षणे ॥ २.१०३.२१॥
21.en: All the queens treated Lakshmana, born of Dasaratha and endowed with auspicious qualities, with the same love as they did to Rama.
21.hi: उनके पास ही तरकसों में भरे सुय की किरणों के समान चरुकीले एत्र भयङ्कर वाण शोभा दे रहे थे। मानों चसकीले फलों बाले (मशियुक्त होने के कारण) सर्पो से भोगवती नाञ्जी नगरी सुशोखित. हा

22.sa: सीतापि चरणांस्तासामुपसंगृह्य दु:खिता ।श्वश्रूणामश्रुपूर्णाक्षी सा बभूवाग्रत: स्थिता ॥ २.१०३.२२॥
22.en: Sita, too, overcome with grief, grasped the feet of her mothersinlaw and stood before them, her eyes full of tears.
22.hi: बहाँ पर दो तलवारे भो रखी थीं, जिनकी सोमे की म्यानें शीं और उनके पास ही दो ढालें भी रखी थीं जिन पर सोने के फूल बने हुए थे

23.sa: तां परिष्वज्य दु:खार्त्तां माता दुहितरं यथा ।वनवासकृशां दीनां कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ २.१०३.२३॥
23.en: Like a mother to her daughter, Kausalya embraced the wretched Sita, who was afflicted with sorrow, and emaciated due to her stay in the forest, and said to her:
23.hi: वहाँ कितन ही गोधा के चाम क और काऽचनभूपित तरह तरह के झंगुलित्राण ( दस्ताने ) भी थे । जिस पणशाल्ला में इंस प्रकार के शत्र रखे थे,वह शत्रुओं द्वारा उसी प्रकार अभेद्य थी, जिस प्रकार सिंह की गुफा, हरनों के झु डों के लिए अभेद्य होती है

24.sa: विदेहराजस्य सुता स्नुषा दशरथस्य च ।रामपत्नी कथं दु:खं सम्प्राप्ता निर्जने वने ॥ २.१०३.२४॥
24.en: How is it that Sita, daughter of Janaka, king of Videha, daughterinlaw of Dasaratha and wife of Rama, has to undergo such hardships in the lonely forest.

25.sa: पद्ममातपसन्तप्तं परिक्लिष्टमिवोत्पलम् ।काञ्चनं रजसा ध्वस्तं क्लिष्टं चन्द्रमिवाम्बुदै: ॥ २.१०३.२५॥
25.en: O Sita, after looking at your countenance, which is like a lotus, scorched by the sunshine, or like a withered waterlily or gold defiled by dust or the Moon obscured by the clouds, the fire of sorrow is burning my mind. The grief in my mind is like fire kindled from the arani (sacrificial faggots) that consumes its own souree. (On a circular wood piece, a wooden stick is placed and churned to produce fire specially in sacrifices is called arani.)
25.hi: भरत जी एक मुहूर्त तक ता पणराजा की बनावट और सजावट देखते रहे, तदनन्तर उन्होंने पण शाला में बैठे हुए और जटाजूट धारण किए हुए बड़े भाई को देखा

26.sa: मुखं ते प्रेक्ष्य मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाश्रयम् भृशं मनसि वैदेहि व्यसनारणिसम्भव: ॥ २.१०३.२६॥
26.en: O Sita, after looking at your countenance, which is like a lotus, scorched by the sunshine, or like a withered waterlily or gold defiled by dust or the Moon obscured by the clouds, the fire of sorrow is burning my mind. The grief in my mind is like fire kindled from the arani (sacrificial faggots) that consumes its own souree. (On a circular wood piece, a wooden stick is placed and churned to produce fire specially in sacrifices is called arani.)
26.hi: अरत जी ने अग्नि की तरह (दुदर्श) श्रीशम को ऊपर से काळे हिरन का चाम ओइ ओर कमर पर ( धोती की जगह ) चीर बल्कल पहिने हुए, कुटी के पास ही बेठा देखा

27.sa: ब्रुवन्त्यामेवमार्त्तायां जनन्यां भरताग्रज: ।पादावासाद्य जग्राह वसिष्ठस्य च राघव: ॥ २.१०३.२७॥
27.en: While Rama's mother was uttering such words in anguish, Rama reached Vasistha and clasped his feet with reverence.
27.hi: उनकी भुजाएँ घुटनों तक लंबी, उनके कंघे सिंह के कधों के समान ऊँचे और नेत्र कमज के समान थे | वे ससागरा प्रथिवी के स्वामी और साथ ही धर्मचारी भी थे

28.sa: पुरोहितस्याग्निसमस्य वै तदा बृहस्पतेरिन्द्र इवामराधिप: ।प्रगृह्य पादौ सुसमृद्धतेजस: सहैव तेनोपविवेश राघव: ॥ २.१०३.२८॥
28.en: Rama touched the feet of the family priest Vasistha, a man equivalent to effulgent fire like Indra, the lord of the gods, does to Brihaspati and sat down along with him.
28.hi: उनको भरत ने सीता और लक्ष्मण के साथ एक चबूतरे पर, कुशा के आसन के ऊपर, शाश्वत ब्रह्म की तरह, बैठा हुआ देखा

29.sa: ततो जघन्यं सहितै: समन्त्रिभि: पुरप्रधानैश्च सहैव सैनिकै: ।जनेन धर्मज्ञतमेन धर्मवानुपोपविष्टो भरतस्तदाग्रजम् ॥ २.१०३.२९॥
29.en: After Vasistha and Rama sat down, righteous Bharata sat close to his elder brother. Behind him sat his companions, leading citizens, soldiers and righteous men.

30.sa: उपोपविष्टस्तु तथा स वीर्यवांस्तपस्विवेषेण समीक्ष्य राघवम् ।श्रिया ज्वलन्तं भरत: कृताञ्जलिर्यथा महेन्द्र: प्रयत: प्रजापतिम् ॥ २.१०३.३०॥
30.en: Beholding Rama attired like an ascetic but radiant with a majestic glow, the extremely valiant Bharata sat near him with folded palms like the great Indra purified by religious austerities sits near Brahma, the creator.
30.hi: श्रीराम को ( इस प्रकार ) बैठा हुआ देख कैकेयीतन्दन धर्मात्मा भरत, दुःख से विकल हो, उनकी ओर दोड़े २६ ॥ अऋभितः-समीपे । ( रा० ) इृष्टेब विललापातों बाष्पसन्दिग्धया गिरा । अशक्लुतरन्धारयित्‌' धैर्याद्चनमन्रवीत्‌

31.sa: किमेष वाक्यं भरतो ऽद्य राघवं प्रणम्य सत्कृत्य च साधु वक्ष्यति ।इतीव तस्यार्यजनस्य तत्त्वतो बभूव कौतूहलमुत्तमं तदा ॥ २.१०३.३१॥
31.en: All noble people were truly filled with great curiosity as to what Bharata was going to speak, after paying his homage and honouring Rama.

32.sa: स राघव: सत्यधृतिश्च लक्ष्मणो महानुभवो भरतश्च धार्मिक: ।वृता: सुहृद्भिश्च विरेजुरध्वरे यथा सदस्यै: सहितास्त्रयो ऽग्नय: ॥ २.१०३.३२ ॥
32.en: Rama who was steadfast in truth, Lakshmana of great dignity and righteous Bharata surrounded by their friends were as resplendent as three sacrificial fires encircled by officiating priests. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्य्रुत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredthird sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
32.hi: हाय ! जो राजसभा में बैठ मंत्रियों द्वारा उपासनां किए जाने योग्य हैं बह भेरा बड़ा भाई, आज बन्यमृगों द्वारा उपासित हो, बैठा है । अर्थात जो श्रीरामचन्द्र राजसभा में मंत्रियों के बीच बैठने योग्य हैं, वे बनजन्तुओं के बीच बैठे हुए हैं ३१ ॥ वासो भिर्ष हुसाहस्ले योरे महात्मा पुरोचितः । मृगाजिने सोज्यमिह प्रशस्ते धर्ममाचरन्‌

33.hi: संसदि-सभायां। ( गो० ) २ युक्तः-ग्रहः । ( गो० ) ३ -बहुसाहस्थो:--बहुसहसमूल्ये: | ( गो० ) CN जो सदा तरह तरह के चित्र विचित्र पुष्पों की मालाएँ धारण करत थे, वही श्रीराम आज इस जटाभार को किस-प्रकार सहन कर रहे हें

34.hi: जिसको ऋषि द्वारा यथाविधि किए गए यज्ञा से पुण्यसञ्चय करना उचित था वह श्रीराम अपने ही शरीर को कष्ट दे कर युण्यसञचय कर रहा हे

35.hi: जिसके शारीर म वांढ्या चन्दन का.लेप किआ जाता था, उस मेरे ज्येछ्ठ भ्राता का शरीर देखो तो कैसा मैला हो रहा है

36.hi: हा ! मेरे ही पीछे, सुखों का उपभोग करने वाले श्रीराम यह कष्ट भोग रहे हैं. ! हा ! मुक नृशंस और लोकनिन्दित मेरे इस जीवन को धिक्कार हे

37.hi: इस प्रकार विलाप करते हुए भरत, दुःखी थे । उनका मुख- कमल पसीने से तर था। उन्होंने चाहा कि, दौड़ कर श्रीराम चरणों में गिरे, किन्तु बहाँ तक न पहुँच, वे रो कर बीच ही में मूछित हो गिर पडे

40.hi: रोते हुए शत्रुघ्न ने श्रीरामचन्द्र जी के चरणों को प्रणाम किआ । तब श्रीरामचन्द्र जी इन दोनों भाइयों को छाती से लगा, स्वयं रोने लगे

1.sa: तं तु राम: समाज्ञाय भ्रातरं गुरुवत्सलम् ।लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे ॥ २.१०४.१॥
1.en: Rama with his brother Lakshmana having consoled Bharata who is ever devoted to elders began to question:
